summary: Parse one validated Pleiades extended EQDSK text file.

identity.relation: Deterministic text serialization/deserialization of Pleiades EQDSK records
identity.direction: extended EQDSK text and validated dictionary/class state
identity.definition: 48-character title, four integer fields, four 5-value scalar records, five profiles, C-order psi grid, q profile and fixed-width limiter/vessel coordinate pairs
identity.model: Pleiades legacy extended dialect retained from D0 lexical successor
identity.geometry: nnr by nnz grid reconstructed as R linspace(0,rbox) and Z linspace(-zbox/2,zbox/2)
identity.coordinates: R/Z coordinate values in source-defined convention; units and COCOS unspecified
identity.boundary: Unlike official EFIT G-EQDSK: this dialect has 48-character title + four ints, nnr/nnz/nnv, and no magnetic-axis scalar contract.
assumptions: Finite real values and fixed-width coordinate fields
This is not standard EFIT gEQDSK

inputs.name: strict
inputs.description: Reject trailing records after declared section
inputs.constraints: False allows trailing only, not missing fields

failure_semantics.invalid_input: EQDSKFormatError before destination truncation for writer validation or malformed reader records.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Filesystem errors propagate; parse errors are EQDSKFormatError.
failure_semantics.partial_results: Class wrapper preserves previous mapping when a read fails.

example.description: Build a minimal fixed-width Pleiades EQDSK text file and read its 2-by-2 psi records.
example.code:
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
from scirel.io.eqdsk import read_pleiades_eqdsk
lines = ['MANUAL EXAMPLE'.ljust(48) + '   1   2   2   2']
for values in [[1., 2., 0., 0., 0.]] + [[0.]*5]*3 + [[1., 2.]]*4 + [[1., 2., 3., 4.], [0., 0.]]:
    lines.append(''.join('%16.9E' % value for value in values))
lines.append('    0    0')
with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory)/'example.eqdsk'
    path.write_text('\n'.join(lines)+'\n')
    parsed = read_pleiades_eqdsk(path)
    assert parsed['psi'].tolist() == [[1., 2.], [3., 4.]]
example.expected: The parser returns psi=[[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]] in declared order.

scope: Roundtrip, lexical fixed-width, malformed input and class-state tests
verification.evidence_ceiling: Structural IO qualification only; no physical interpretation or release approval.
known_limitations: This reader does not select raw contours or write them; the separate write-pleiades-eqdsk-legacy-raw contract defines that bounded writer qualification
